To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
corticotropinreleasing factor and PGE2 sequentially activate the brainstem neurons to induce an increase in the sympathetic nerve activity to the spleen.
the CRF and PEGE2 in the brain sequentially activate the splenic sympathetic nervous system in rats, and the activation of CRF system is dependent on the activation of PGE system.
corticotropin releasing factor and prostaglandin-E2 are sequentially activated in the brain to increase the sympathetic nerve activity in the spleen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CRF and prostaglandin in the brain on the splenic sympathetic nervous system.
the role of the central CRF system in mediating splenic sympathetic nerve activation.
the sequential relationship of the actions of CRF in the brain and PGE2 system in the brain on sympathetic nerve activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CRF-induced activation of the splenic nerve activity was mediated by PGE2.
CRF and PEG2 are sequentially involved in the central regulation of the splenic efferent activity.

the splenic sympathetic nervous system is under the control of the brain CRF and PEG2 system, and that the brain CRF system plays a role in the control of the splenic sympathetics by acting sequentially to PGE2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CRF system in brain is involved in the regulation of the sympathetic outflow to the spleen via the prostaglandin system.
the CRF-induced increase in the splanic sympathetic nerve activity is mediated by the CRF receptor, and that PGE2 is involved in the CRF-induced activation of the sympathetic nerve.
CRF in the brain is involved in a control of splenic sympathetic nerve activities via PGE2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CRF can be used to increase sympathetic tone in the splenic nerve, which is a key component of the stress response.
the CRF-PGE2 pathway may play a role in regulating sympathetic activity in the splenic nerve.
the brain CRF-PGE2 axis is involved in the regulation of splenic sympathetic nerve activities.
